text.title: C# .NET Core Backend Worked Examples
text.summary: Worked examples for the four layers this umbrella scaffolds — controller, EF Core entity configuration, channel-backed background service, and the xUnit unit/integration pair — followed by the manifest the methodology emits.

example.note: Two constructor dependencies, both interfaces (constructor-inject-interfaces-only). ActionResult<T> plus CreatedAtAction on create (apicontroller-actionresult). CancellationToken last on every action (cancellation-token-plumbing). Returns record DTOs, never entities (record-dtos-not-entities).
Mapping lives outside the entity (entity-type-configuration-classes); the domain type stays free of EF attributes.
AsNoTracking on a read, AsSplitQuery because two collection Includes would otherwise multiply rows, materialised before returning, PagedResult instead of IQueryable (ef-asnotracking-on-reads).

antipattern.reason: The caller can append arbitrary LINQ that bypasses the repository's constraints, and the query executes after the DbContext scope is gone.

example.note: Scope created per work item, so the singleton never captures the scoped DbContext (di-lifetimes); the channel is bounded, so back-pressure is explicit (channel-and-periodictimer-for-background-work).
WaitForNextTickAsync holds the wall-clock interval without drift and returns false on cancellation, so shutdown needs no extra coordination.

Interface mocked, ActionResult shape asserted before the value is read; the integration class shares one in-process server through IClassFixture and CreateClient (moq-interfaces-and-classfixture-tests, program-partial-for-webapplicationfactory).
